spec.description: Where each ancestry group clusters, state by state: global and local Moran's I (LISA) of a group's share across census tracts, with a Moran scatter plot, histograms and the reference distribution of Moran's I drawn by Mosaic and linked to the maps, computed in the browser from the ACS 2024.

options.content:
**Data.** The share of each census tract's residents who report an ancestry or origin, from the American Community Survey 2020–2024 five-year estimates (tables B04006, B03001, B02015; published by the U.S. Census Bureau in 2025, public domain), with the tract polygons of the TIGER 2024 cartographic boundary files, built once per instance by `datasets/ancestry/build.sh`. Tracts with fewer than 100 residents are left out (about 650 of 85,044): a share of 30 people swings by a third with one household. ACS margins of error are not used.

**Neighbours.** Built in the same step from the polygons as published, within each state. *Queen contiguity*: two tracts touch at a border or a corner (a tract with none is an island and gets no LISA). *6 nearest*: the six tracts with the nearest interior points, which links islands but not symmetrically. Weights are row-standardised, so a tract's spatial lag is the mean of its neighbours' values.

**Statistics.** Global Moran's I with its expectation and variance under randomisation, and its reference distribution: I again with the shares shuffled among the tracts, as many times as *Permutations* says, as PySAL's `esda.Moran` gets its pseudo p-value. Local Moran's I for every tract, with a pseudo p-value from conditional permutations: the tract keeps its value and its neighbours are replaced by tracts drawn at random from the rest of the state, as many times as *Permutations* says. As in PySAL, each permutation draws one random set shared by all tracts, without replacement; the draws come from a hash, so every visit gets the same p-values. Checked against PySAL esda 2.10 on Illinois and California: the same I, z and local I to 14 digits, and counts of significant tracts within the spread of PySAL's own permutation runs.

**Reading it.** A LISA map is exploratory, not a test of segregation: with thousands of tracts some pass p ≤ 0.05 by chance (pick *FDR 5 %* to control that), the clusters depend on the neighbours chosen and on the tracts' size and shape, and a share says nothing about where people choose to live. ACS ancestry is self-reported and multiple-response. The scatter plot and the histograms are drawn by [Mosaic](https://idl.uw.edu/mosaic/) on the same browser tables as everything else.

options.content:
# Where ancestry groups cluster

Exploratory spatial data analysis of the **American Community Survey 2024**, one state at a time: is a group's share of residents high where its neighbours' is high too? **Moran's I** answers for the whole state; **local Moran's I** (LISA) finds where: the *High-High* hot spots, the *Low-Low* cold spots, and the outliers that differ from the tracts around them. Everything is computed in your browser, with the same method as [PySAL](https://pysal.org/esda/) and [GeoDa](https://geodacenter.github.io/).

**Drag a box on the scatter plot**, or a range on the share histogram, to select the tracts in it: both maps dim the rest and the histograms show where the selection falls. **Click a tract** on a map to find it on the plot, **Shift+click** to add more, click empty map to clear. Change the neighbours, the permutations or the significance to see how much the clusters depend on them.

spec.rawSql:
-- The cluster map: every tract coloured by its LISA cluster (dataset clusters).
-- `selected` is the box brushed on the scatter plot and the share histogram, which the map marks and
-- dims the rest around (selectionField). The tracts clicked one by one (sel)
-- the map rings by itself; filtering on either would leave nothing to dim.
SELECT c.geoid, s.name, s.county, round(c.share, 2) AS share, c.cluster, round(c.p, 3) AS p,
       coalesce((try_cast($bx0 AS DOUBLE) IS NOT NULL OR try_cast($sh0 AS DOUBLE) IS NOT NULL)
         AND (try_cast($bx0 AS DOUBLE) IS NULL OR (c.z BETWEEN try_cast($bx0 AS DOUBLE) AND try_cast($bx1 AS DOUBLE) AND c.lag BETWEEN try_cast($by0 AS DOUBLE) AND try_cast($by1 AS DOUBLE)))
         AND (try_cast($sh0 AS DOUBLE) IS NULL OR c.share BETWEEN try_cast($sh0 AS DOUBLE) AND try_cast($sh1 AS DOUBLE)), false) AS selected, s.geojson
FROM $clusters c JOIN $shapes s USING (geoid)

spec.description: The LISA cluster map: each tract coloured by its local Moran's I quadrant where the pseudo p-value clears the significance picked, from conditional permutations. Only significant tracts get a colour; a cluster's core is the coloured tract, its neighbours are part of the pattern too. Click a tract to select it, Shift+click to add one; the rest of the map dims around the selection.
spec.title: Local clusters · ${grupo} in ${state:text}

spec.rawSql:
-- Global Moran's I over the tracts of $lisa, with its expectation and
-- variance under randomisation (Cliff and Ord 1981), as PySAL's esda.Moran
-- reports them (EI, VI_rand, z_rand, p_rand two-sided). Row-standardised
-- weights w_ij = 1/k_i; S0, S1 and S2 are the usual sums over them.
WITH t AS (
  SELECT geoid, z, lag, k FROM $lisa
),
w AS (
  SELECT l.i, l.j, 1.0 / count(*) OVER (PARTITION BY l.i) AS wij
  FROM $links l
  WHERE l.i IN (SELECT geoid FROM t) AND l.j IN (SELECT geoid FROM t)
),
pairs AS (
  SELECT coalesce(a.wij, 0) + coalesce(b.wij, 0) AS s
  FROM w a FULL JOIN w b ON a.i = b.j AND a.j = b.i
),
margins AS (
  SELECT t.geoid, CASE WHEN t.k > 0 THEN 1.0 ELSE 0.0 END AS row_sum,
         coalesce((SELECT sum(w.wij) FROM w WHERE w.j = t.geoid), 0) AS col_sum
  FROM t
),
s AS (
  SELECT (SELECT count(*) FROM t) AS n,
         (SELECT count(*) FILTER (WHERE k > 0) FROM t)::DOUBLE AS s0,
         (SELECT 0.5 * sum(s * s) FROM pairs) AS s1,
         (SELECT sum(power(row_sum + col_sum, 2)) FROM margins) AS s2,
         (SELECT sum(z * lag) FILTER (WHERE k > 0) FROM t) AS zlag,
         (SELECT sum(z * z) FROM t) AS z2,
         (SELECT sum(power(z, 4)) FROM t) AS z4
),
m AS (
  SELECT n, s0, s1, s2,
         n / s0 * zlag / z2 AS i,
         -1.0 / (n - 1) AS ei,
         n * z4 / (z2 * z2) AS b2
  FROM s
),
v AS (
  SELECT *,
         (n * ((n * n - 3 * n + 3) * s1 - n * s2 + 3 * s0 * s0)
          - b2 * ((n * n - n) * s1 - 2 * n * s2 + 6 * s0 * s0))
         / ((n - 1) * (n - 2) * (n - 3) * s0 * s0) - ei * ei AS vi
  FROM m
),
zz AS (
  SELECT *, (i - ei) / sqrt(vi) AS z_rand FROM v
),
-- Two-sided p from the normal tail, by Abramowitz and Stegun's erfc 7.1.26
-- (error below 1.5e-7): DuckDB has no erf.
tail AS (
  SELECT *, abs(z_rand) / sqrt(2) AS x, 1 / (1 + 0.3275911 * abs(z_rand) / sqrt(2)) AS t FROM zz
),
res AS (
  SELECT *, t * (0.254829592 + t * (-0.284496736 + t * (1.421413741 + t * (-1.453152027 + t * 1.061405429))))
            * exp(-x * x) AS p_rand
  FROM tail
)
SELECT round(i, 3) AS "Moran's I", round(z_rand, 1) AS "z",
       CASE WHEN p_rand < 0.001 THEN '< 0.001' ELSE printf('%.3f', p_rand) END AS "p",
       n::DOUBLE AS "Tracts"
FROM res

spec.description: Moran's I of the group's share across the state's tracts, with row-standardised weights, and its z-score and two-sided p under randomisation (Cliff and Ord), as PySAL's esda.Moran reports them. Near 0: no spatial pattern; towards 1: tracts with similar shares sit together; below 0: neighbours tend to differ.

spec.rawSql:
-- Pooled shares: the group's residents over all residents, not a mean of tract shares.
WITH sel AS (SELECT unnest([${sel:singlequote}]::VARCHAR[]) AS geoid),
picked AS (
  -- the selection: tracts picked one by one (sel), and the box brushed on the scatter
  -- plot and the share histogram (both, when both are)
  SELECT c.geoid FROM $clusters c
  WHERE c.geoid IN (SELECT geoid FROM sel) OR coalesce((try_cast($bx0 AS DOUBLE) IS NOT NULL OR try_cast($sh0 AS DOUBLE) IS NOT NULL)
         AND (try_cast($bx0 AS DOUBLE) IS NULL OR (c.z BETWEEN try_cast($bx0 AS DOUBLE) AND try_cast($bx1 AS DOUBLE) AND c.lag BETWEEN try_cast($by0 AS DOUBLE) AND try_cast($by1 AS DOUBLE)))
         AND (try_cast($sh0 AS DOUBLE) IS NULL OR c.share BETWEEN try_cast($sh0 AS DOUBLE) AND try_cast($sh1 AS DOUBLE)), false)
),
t AS (SELECT v.geoid, v.people, s.total_pop FROM $tractvals v JOIN $shapes s USING (geoid))
SELECT (SELECT count(*) FROM picked)::DOUBLE AS "Selected",
       (SELECT 100 * sum(people) / nullif(sum(total_pop), 0) FROM t WHERE geoid IN (SELECT geoid FROM picked)) AS "Their share",
       (SELECT 100 * sum(people) / sum(total_pop) FROM t) AS "State"

WITH sel AS (SELECT unnest([${sel:singlequote}]::VARCHAR[]) AS geoid),
picked AS (
  -- the selection: tracts picked one by one (sel), and the box brushed on the scatter
  -- plot and the share histogram (both, when both are)
  SELECT c.geoid FROM $clusters c
  WHERE c.geoid IN (SELECT geoid FROM sel) OR coalesce((try_cast($bx0 AS DOUBLE) IS NOT NULL OR try_cast($sh0 AS DOUBLE) IS NOT NULL)
         AND (try_cast($bx0 AS DOUBLE) IS NULL OR (c.z BETWEEN try_cast($bx0 AS DOUBLE) AND try_cast($bx1 AS DOUBLE) AND c.lag BETWEEN try_cast($by0 AS DOUBLE) AND try_cast($by1 AS DOUBLE)))
         AND (try_cast($sh0 AS DOUBLE) IS NULL OR c.share BETWEEN try_cast($sh0 AS DOUBLE) AND try_cast($sh1 AS DOUBLE)), false)
)
SELECT replace(s.name, 'Census Tract ', '') AS "Tract", replace(s.county, ' County', '') AS "County",
       c.share AS "Share %", c.lag AS "Neighbours' z", c.p AS "p", c.cluster AS "Cluster"
FROM $clusters c JOIN $shapes s USING (geoid)
WHERE CASE WHEN (SELECT count(*) FROM picked) > 0
           THEN c.geoid IN (SELECT geoid FROM picked)
           ELSE c.cluster IN ('High-High', 'High-Low') END
ORDER BY c.p, c.share DESC
LIMIT 1000

query.rawSql:
-- Server side, once per state: the outline of every tract the analysis covers
-- (those of at least 100 residents, which is every tract the weights list:
-- datasets/ancestry/build.sql, step 7), as GeoJSON text for the maps, with its
-- name, county and population.
SELECT t.geoid, t.name, t.county, t.total_pop::DOUBLE AS total_pop,
       CAST(ST_AsGeoJSON(g.geometry) AS VARCHAR) AS geojson
FROM read_parquet('http://feeds/datasets/ancestry/tracts.parquet') t
JOIN read_parquet('http://feeds/datasets/ancestry/tracts-geom.parquet') g USING (geoid)
WHERE t.geoid IN (SELECT i FROM read_parquet('http://feeds/datasets/ancestry/weights.parquet') WHERE kind = 'knn6' AND state = $state)

-- Server side, once per state and group: the group's share of each tract's
-- residents, in %, and 0 where the ACS counts none of them (it leaves those
-- rows out). The value every statistic below is computed on.
SELECT t.geoid, 100 * coalesce(a.pct, 0) AS share, coalesce(a.estimate, 0)::DOUBLE AS people
FROM read_parquet('http://feeds/datasets/ancestry/tracts.parquet') t
LEFT JOIN read_parquet('http://feeds/datasets/ancestry/tract-ancestry.parquet') a ON a.geoid = t.geoid AND a.ancestry = $grupo
WHERE t.geoid IN (SELECT i FROM read_parquet('http://feeds/datasets/ancestry/weights.parquet') WHERE kind = 'knn6' AND state = $state)

-- Server side, once per state and kind of neighbours: who neighbours whom, as
-- directed pairs (i, j), built from the tract polygons by
-- datasets/ancestry/build.sql, step 7. Queen: sharing a border or a corner;
-- knn6: the six nearest.
SELECT i, j FROM read_parquet('http://feeds/datasets/ancestry/weights.parquet') WHERE kind = $weights AND state = $state

source.sql:
-- Local Moran's I (LISA) for every tract, in the browser, from two datasets:
-- $tractvals (geoid, share) and $links (i, j: who neighbours whom). Weights
-- are row-standardised, as GeoDa and PySAL use by default: a tract's spatial
-- lag is the mean z of its neighbours. ii is PySAL's Is, (n - 1) z lag / sum z².
--
-- Significance by conditional permutation (Anselin 1995), the way PySAL's
-- esda does it: each permutation draws one random set of k_max positions among
-- the n - 1 "other" tracts, shared by every tract, and tract i reads the first
-- k_i of them as its neighbours. Without replacement. The set is the k_max
-- positions with the smallest hash(permutation, position), not random(), so
-- every load and every viewer gets the same p-values. With the sets shared, a
-- permuted lag is a prefix sum of the set, and only the few permutations
-- whose set contains i's own position need a correction (the n-th tract
-- stands in for it: "others" of i are positions 1..n with i's swapped for n).
WITH x AS (
  SELECT geoid, share AS x FROM $tractvals
),
z AS (
  SELECT geoid, x,
         (x - avg(x) OVER ()) / nullif(stddev_pop(x) OVER (), 0) AS z,
         row_number() OVER (ORDER BY geoid) AS rn
  FROM x
),
w AS (
  SELECT i, j, 1.0 / count(*) OVER (PARTITION BY i) AS wij
  FROM $links
  WHERE i IN (SELECT geoid FROM z) AND j IN (SELECT geoid FROM z)
),
lag AS (
  SELECT w.i AS geoid, sum(w.wij * z.z) AS lag, count(*) AS k
  FROM w JOIN z ON z.geoid = w.j
  GROUP BY w.i
),
obs AS (
  SELECT z.geoid, z.x, z.z, z.rn, lag.lag, coalesce(lag.k, 0) AS k
  FROM z LEFT JOIN lag USING (geoid)
),
n AS (
  SELECT count(*) AS n, max(k) AS kmax, max(rn) AS last FROM obs
),
perms AS (
  SELECT coalesce(try_cast($perms AS BIGINT), 499) AS p
),
sets AS (
  -- 64 is a ceiling on k_max: the most neighbours any tract has is 34 (queen)
  SELECT s.p, min_by(m.m, hash(s.p * 4294967296 + m.m), 64) AS picks
  FROM perms, range(perms.p) s(p), n, range(1, n.n) m(m)
  GROUP BY s.p
),
draws AS (
  SELECT p, unnest(picks) AS pick, generate_subscripts(picks, 1) AS r FROM sets
),
prefix AS (
  -- the sum of z over the first k picks of each permutation
  SELECT d.p, d.r AS k, sum(z.z) OVER (PARTITION BY d.p ORDER BY d.r) AS s
  FROM draws d JOIN z ON z.rn = d.pick
  WHERE d.r <= (SELECT kmax FROM n)
),
own AS (
  -- the permutations whose first k_i picks hit tract i's own position
  SELECT o.rn, d.p
  FROM draws d JOIN obs o ON o.rn = d.pick AND d.r <= o.k
),
sim AS (
  SELECT o.rn,
         count_if(o.z * (pf.s + CASE WHEN own.p IS NULL THEN 0 ELSE stand_in.z - o.z END) / o.k
                  >= o.z * o.lag) AS larger
  FROM obs o
  JOIN prefix pf ON pf.k = o.k
  LEFT JOIN own ON own.rn = o.rn AND own.p = pf.p
  CROSS JOIN (SELECT z.z FROM z, n WHERE z.rn = n.last) stand_in
  WHERE o.k > 0
  GROUP BY o.rn
)
SELECT o.geoid, o.x AS share, o.z, o.lag, o.k,
       (n.n - 1) * o.z * o.lag / n.n AS ii,
       (least(s.larger, perms.p - s.larger) + 1) / (perms.p + 1) AS p,
       CASE WHEN o.k = 0 THEN 'none'
            WHEN o.z >= 0 AND o.lag >= 0 THEN 'HH'
            WHEN o.z < 0 AND o.lag < 0 THEN 'LL'
            WHEN o.z >= 0 THEN 'HL'
            ELSE 'LH' END AS quadrant
FROM obs o
LEFT JOIN sim s USING (rn)
CROSS JOIN n
CROSS JOIN perms

-- What the maps and charts colour by: each tract's LISA quadrant where its
-- pseudo p-value clears the significance picked, "Not significant" where it
-- does not. FDR is Benjamini and Hochberg's false discovery rate at 5 %, over
-- the tracts with neighbours: with thousands of tests, p ≤ 0.05 alone lets
-- about one tract in twenty through by chance.
WITH tested AS (
  SELECT p, row_number() OVER (ORDER BY p) AS rnk, count(*) OVER () AS m
  FROM $lisa WHERE k > 0
),
cut AS (
  SELECT CASE WHEN $alpha = 'fdr'
              THEN coalesce((SELECT max(p) FROM tested WHERE p <= 0.05 * rnk / m), 0)
              ELSE coalesce(try_cast($alpha AS DOUBLE), 0.05) END AS cut
)
SELECT l.geoid, l.share, l.z, l.lag, l.k, l.ii, l.p, cut.cut,
       CASE WHEN l.k = 0 THEN 'No neighbours'
            WHEN l.p > cut.cut THEN 'Not significant'
            WHEN l.quadrant = 'HH' THEN 'High-High'
            WHEN l.quadrant = 'LL' THEN 'Low-Low'
            WHEN l.quadrant = 'HL' THEN 'High-Low'
            ELSE 'Low-High' END AS cluster
FROM $lisa l, cut
-- the significant tracts last, so the Mosaic scatter plot draws them on top
ORDER BY l.p DESC

-- The reference distribution of global Moran's I: I again for each
-- permutation of the z values among the tracts (all of them, islands too), as
-- PySAL's esda.Moran draws its pseudo p-value. Permutation p puts at position
-- rn the z of the tract ranked rn by hash(p, rn), not random(), so every visit
-- gets the same distribution. I = n / S0 * sum w_ij z_i z_j / sum z^2 with
-- row-standardised weights, as the Global Moran's I panel computes it.
-- Each permutation is one list of z read by position: a join per link and
-- permutation would cost five times as long.
WITH t AS (
  SELECT geoid, z, k, row_number() OVER (ORDER BY geoid) AS rn FROM $lisa
),
s AS (
  SELECT count(*) AS n, count(*) FILTER (WHERE k > 0)::DOUBLE AS s0, sum(z * z) AS z2 FROM t
),
w AS (
  SELECT a.rn AS ri, b.rn AS rj, 1.0 / count(*) OVER (PARTITION BY l.i) AS wij
  FROM $links l JOIN t a ON a.geoid = l.i JOIN t b ON b.geoid = l.j
),
perms AS (
  SELECT coalesce(try_cast($perms AS BIGINT), 499) AS p
),
shuffled AS (
  SELECT q.p, list(t.z ORDER BY hash(q.p * 4294967296 + t.rn)) AS zs
  FROM perms, range(perms.p) q(p), t
  GROUP BY q.p
),
ip AS (
  SELECT p, sum(w.wij * zs[w.ri] * zs[w.rj]) AS zlag FROM shuffled, w GROUP BY p
),
obs AS (
  SELECT sum(w.wij * a.z * b.z) AS zlag FROM w JOIN t a ON a.rn = w.ri JOIN t b ON b.rn = w.rj
)
SELECT ip.p AS perm, s.n / s.s0 * ip.zlag / s.z2 AS i, s.n / s.s0 * obs.zlag / s.z2 AS observed
FROM ip, s, obs
